title: Wells Fargo, HUD and the Fight Over Black Homeownership Programs | Across the Water, Ep. 21
lede: Black homeownership fell to 44.4% in the third quarter of 2026, from 45.7% a year earlier, while white homeownership rose to 75.1% (Census Bureau). HUD opened a Fair Housing Act probe into Wells Fargo's Black homeownership commitments and special purpose credit program on Oct 7, 2026. On Nov 18, 20 attorneys general wrote to the bank to defend those programs as lawful. This episode explains the gap, the pledge, the law behind special purpose credit programs, each side's position, and what it means for Black wealth.
keyPoints: Black homeownership was 44.4% in Q3 2026, down from 45.7% in Q3 2025; non-Hispanic white homeownership rose to 75.1%, a 30.7-point gap (US Census Bureau, Oct 28, 2026).

Wells Fargo pledged in 2017 to lend $60 billion to create 250,000 African American homeowners by 2027, and in 2022 added $210 million for racial equity in homeownership and a $150 million special purpose credit program (Wells Fargo; HousingWire).

HUD opened a Fair Housing Act investigation on Oct 7, 2026. Assistant Secretary Craig Trainor said the Act forbids racial discrimination whatever a program is called; Secretary Scott Turner called dividing Americans by race immoral. No charge has been filed (HousingWire).

On Nov 18, 2026, 20 attorneys general (19 states and DC) told Wells Fargo the programs are lawful: Congress authorized special purpose credit programs in the 1976 Equal Credit Opportunity Act amendments (Maryland Attorney General).

A CFPB rule in force since Jul 21, 2026 bars for-profit lenders' credit programs from using race to decide eligibility; the National Fair Housing Alliance and the National Urban League have sued to overturn it (Federal Register; Maryland Attorney General).
